Job DescriptionHVDC Primary & Valve Installation Supervisor (m/f/d)

GE Vernova is facing a momentum of hypergrowth, and we are currently scaling up our teams, creating others from scratch, and bringing our industry to the next level. Join us on this mission!

At GE Vernova Grid Solutions we are electrifying the world with advanced grid technologies. As leaders in the energy space our goal is to accelerate the transition for a more energy efficient grid to full fill the needs of tomorrow. With a focus on growth and sustainability GE Vernova Grid Solutions plays a pivotable role in integrating Renewables onto the grid to drive to carbon neutral.

Due to the growth of our HVDC business, we are currently looking for our next HVDC Primary & Valve Installation Supervisor in the “Construction & Commissioning” function to participate in this energy transition.

Your Mission: Within our large scale HVDC Projects you are responsible for the Supervision of the Installation for our HVDC Valves including the Valve Cooling System. The installation will be done by subcontractors.

This position implies functional leadership as an IC (Individual Contributor) without direct reports. It is a Construction Site based role.

Join us and enjoy playing a major role to enhance the Central Europe Construction & Commissioning function with fresh ideas!

Why we come to work:

At GE Vernova, our employees are always up for the challenge - and we’re always driven to find the best solution. Our projects are unique and interesting, and you’ll need to bring a solution-focused, positive approach to each one to do your best. Surrounded by committed, loyal colleagues, if you can dare to bring your ingenuity and desire to make an impact, you’ll be exposed to game-changing, diverse projects that truly allow you to play your part in the energy transition.
Main Tasks/Responsibilities:

1. EHS
Ensure all installation activities are performed in accordance with safety protocols and regulatory requirements.
2. Quality Oversight
Implement quality control measures to ensure the reliability and performance of installed HVDC Valves & HVDC Primary Equipment.
Conduct inspections based on ITPs to verify adherence to quality standards.
Prepare and review installation documentation, test reports, and as-built drawings.
Ensure all tools, equipment, and materials are properly maintained and stored
3. Planning & Coordination
Coordinate the HVDC Primary Equipment & Valve installation activities with the Site Management Team and other internal and external stakeholders (Installation Subcontractor) on site.
Providing guidance, training and support as needed to the installation subcontractor
Coordinate with our internal Valve manufacturing to assure needed documentation is used at site during execution
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues that arise during the installation process
Technical education, preferably with a degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering or equivalent experience in electrical- or mechanical installation works in large scale projects with at least 3 years experience in the relevant field.
Experience from Supervision or Site Management in substation, FACTS or HVDC Projects preferred.
Strong health and safety mindset aligned with international standards, with the ability to identify and stop unsafe work.
Strong interpersonal, communication, and leadership skills, with the ability to provide clear verbal and written reporting (English required).
Proactive mindset with the ability to recommend and approve corrective actions.
Professional Growth: Dynamic team, extensive resources, and training for skill development
A Booming industry with Cutting-Edge Projects: Involvement in high-profile, innovative projects
Global Exposure: Collaboration with a diverse, global network of industry experts
Collaborative Environment: Supportive culture fostering creativity and teamwork

- translate digital health concepts into scalable solutions, working closely with internal and external stakeholders and continuously optimizing products to maximize adoption, engagement, and long-term impact.

jobs.description:

Your role:
The Director, Global Contamination Control Strategy leads the development, harmonization, and stewardship of microbiological, viral, and environmental contamination control programs across Merck's global manufacturing network, including internal sites and third-party manufacturers (TPMs)/CDMOs. This position reports to the VP, Head of Global Quality Compliance. Acting as the senior global technical authority for contamination control, the successful candidate defines microbial and viral control strategy in close partnership with global and local Engineering, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Quality Control, and Quality Assurance functions, and provides technical direction for new facility start-ups as well as ongoing network operations. The role owns network-level frameworks such as the global Contamination Control Strategy (CCS) methodology, Environmental Monitoring and Cleanroom Performance Qualification (CPQ) standards, contamination FMEA methodology, and contamination response playbooks – establishing a Center of Excellence approach that provides consistent technical direction while allowing for site-specific risk assessment. The Director will build and lead a team of technical experts, mentor site-level microbiology and contamination control staff across the network, and drive continuous improvement through new technologies, digital plant capabilities, and Process Analytical Technology (PAT).

Key Responsibilities:

- Develop and execute a multi-year global roadmap for contamination control and sterility assurance across biologics, small molecules, sterile fill-finish, ADCs, and new modalities.
- Author and maintain global contamination control standards, CCS, EM/CPQ methodology, and contamination FMEA, ensuring harmonized practices reflecting applicable guidance.
- Act as the leading global SME for contamination control and sterility assurance across the network and third-party manufacturers (TPMs)/CDMOs, including during health authority inspections.
- Establish and own the global Environmental Monitoring and CPQ framework, contamination FMEA methodology, and contamination response playbooks; oversee local implementations.
- Provide technical and regulatory guidance on facility design, cleanroom engineering, and microbial/particle control for aseptic and low-bioburden areas.
- Partner with network sites, R&D, and technical development to develop and transfer a robust microbial/viral control strategy across sites; maintain virology controls expertise.
- Develop and mentor the contamination control/microbiology team; share best practices with site teams and senior management.
- Guide cross-functional investigations and trend analyses (water systems, environmental monitoring) to mitigate supply disruptions; apply statistics to define specs and plans.
- Ensure MES/EBR integration for process parameter and monitoring requirements to support regulatory consistency.
- Contribute to global regulatory submissions and responses to health authorities; drive network-wide process improvements including Lean and digitalization.

Who you are:

- 10+ years in sterility assurance, industrial microbiology, or contamination control within a GMP manufacturing environment, with leadership experience.
- Expertise in EU GMP Annex 1, ISO 14644, USP, PDA technical reports, and related regulatory frameworks for aseptic/low-bioburden manufacturing.
- Demonstrated expertise in barrier technology, with a focus on isolator systems, including design, qualification, operational requirements, and regulatory expectations.
- Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
- Willing and able to travel internationally (approximately 20–30%).
- Data-driven with a track record of cross-site collaboration and driving improvements without direct authority.
- Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills across cultures and time zones.
- Hands-on experience with sterile fill-finish operations and cleanroom/facility qualification.
- Experience supporting GMP audits and inspection readiness activities.

About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Job description

In order to support the Airbus Interior Noise department, Airbus Operations is looking for a

Master student in the field of Acoustics - Interior Noise (d/f/m)

You are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of an Acoustics Engineer (d/f/m)? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Interior Noise department as a master student (d/f/m)!

- Location: Hamburg
- Start: 01.01.2027
- Duration: 6 months

We are offering a Master Thesis opportunity focusing on acoustics, specifically interior noise. This role provides a unique chance to contribute to cutting-edge aerospace research and development within a leading global company.

Your location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Your benefits

- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Conducting in-depth research and analysis of interior noise sources and propagation within aircraft cabins.
- Developing and applying advanced simulation models and experimental methodologies for acoustic analysis.
- Evaluating and comparing different noise reduction strategies and materials.* Collecting and analyzing data from various sources, including laboratory tests and flight measurements.
- Documenting research findings and presenting results in a clear and concise manner.
- Collaborating with experienced engineers and researchers within the acoustics department.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Currently enrolled in a Master's degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, Acoustics, or a related field.
- Strong academic record with a focus on acoustics, vibrations, or signal processing.
- Proficiency in relevant software tools (e.g., MATLAB, ANSYS, COMSOL, LMS Test.Lab) is a plus.
- Experience with experimental acoustics and data acquisition systems is beneficial.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Fluency in English (written and spoken) is required; German language skills are a plus.

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

Stellenbeschreibung:
Company Description

In September 2025, AUMOVIO emerged as a spin-off from Continental’s former Automotive group sector and has since established itself as an independent technology company. The company offers a broad portfolio for safe, exciting, connected and autonomous mobility, including sensor solutions, displays, brake and comfort systems as well as extensive expertise in software, architecture platforms and advanced driver assistance systems for software-defined vehicles. In fiscal year 2025, AUMOVIO generated sales of € 18.5 billion. Headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, AUMOVIO has around 82,000 employees at more than 80 locations worldwide.

Job Description

We are looking for an experienced (Senior) Manager - Tax International (m/f/diverse) to join our global tax team based in Frankfurt (hybrid).

In this role, you will be responsible for managing and coordinating all tax-related matters for designated foreign subsidiaries, ensuring compliance with international tax regulations, and driving tax optimization strategies. You will work closely with management, external tax consultants, and fiscal authorities to provide guidance and lead key tax projects across multiple jurisdictions.

Key Responsibilities:

- Providing comprehensive tax guidance for designated foreign countries on corporate income tax, withholding tax and cross-border tax structuring, in close collaboration with the foreign tax functions of the AUMOVIO Group
- Closing collaboration with foreign tax functions, providing ongoing support for business operations
- Providing tax advice and process implementation in tax projects such as liquidations, mergers, acquisitions and restructurings of foreign subsidiaries
- Continuously monitoring, analyzing, developing and implementing changes in German tax legislation with relevance to international tax matters (e.g. CFC rules), monitor global tax developments, including OECD initiatives (e.g. Pillar 2). Assess potential business impacts and develop recommendations to internal stakeholders
- Clearly communicating relevant tax developments, risks, and opportunities to internal stakeholders, including finance, controlling, accounting, legal, and business areas
- Reviewing and assisting foreign tax functions regarding Tax Risk Reporting of foreign subsidiaries
- Supporting and steering the assurance of Pillar II compliance (Global Minimum Tax) requirements, including data collection, impact analysis, and preparation of reporting obligations for designated foreign subsidiaries
- Ensuring adherence to the German Foreign Tax Act (AStG), including foreign CFC rules and outbound taxation requirements
- Overseeing compliance with the DAC (European Directive on Administrative Cooperation) framework, including DAC6 (mandatory disclosure regime) and other relevant reporting obligations
- Developing and maintaining internal processes to secure ongoing compliance with international tax transparency and anti-avoidance regulations
- Preparing and coordinatng responses to German tax audits involving international aspects, e.g. cross-border financing
- Supporting foreign tax functions in tax audits by liaising with local advisors and ensuring consistent global tax positions
- Managing documentation requests and preparing supporting materials for audit defense

Qualifications

- Academic degree in Tax, Finance, Accounting, or a related field; professional tax certifications are a plus (e.g., Steuerberater, CPA, CTA)
- Longterm professional experience in international taxation, ideally in a multinational corporation or a Big Four environment
- Strong understanding of domestic and international tax regulations (e.g., AStG, OECD guidelines)
- Proven experience in working with tax authorities, M&A projects and managing tax matters in multiple jurisdictions
- Business fluent German and English language skills (written and spoken)
- Excellent analytical skills and the ability to translate complex tax concepts into clear business implications
- Ability to work in a team and collaboratively in a global environment
- Willingness to travel

Applications from severely handicapped people are welcome.

• Work on various systems including hydraulic, air conditioning, fuel, engine, cabin components (seats, panels), and electrical systems (routing, crimping, connectors).
• Conduct visual inspections to ensure conformity to safety and quality standards; report any non-conformities or defects.
• Support tasks related to aircraft storage/de-storage.
• Use hand and power tools such as torque wrenches, backing bars, and electrical testing tools.
• Follow FOD rules, internal procedures, and customer standards.
• Ensure compliance with manufacturing and assembly requirements.
• Collaborate in a multicultural environment and assist team members within your area of competence (mechanic, electrical, structure).
• Flexibility to work in shifts (early/late/night) and during weekends when required.

Your profile
• Trained aviation mechanic/electrician with at least 2 years of experience in the aviation sector.
• Experience in both mechanical and electrical systems maintenance and installation.
• Knowledge of Airbus aircraft and procedures is a strong advantage.
• Ability to read and interpret technical documents and engineering drawings.
• Familiar with aviation safety rules, especially FOD regulations.
• Hands-on experience with aircraft systems including engines, hydraulics, fuel, air conditioning, and electrical routing.
• Proficient in using assembly and diagnostic tools (mechanical and electrical).
• Comfortable working at heights; cherry picker/lift machine license is a plus.
• English proficiency level B1 or higher

Your Skills:
• Dynamic, disciplined, and reliable in your work
• Strong initiative and proactive mindset
• Communicative and team-oriented
• Strict adherence to procedures; able to work autonomously
• Solution-focused with the ability to adapt quickly under pressure
• Resilient and calm under stress
